changelog: [When to Segment]: added explicit permissive rule for splitting right after a sentence-initial discourse marker / topic-time adverbial (근데, 그래서, 그러면, 그럼, 이번에는 등) whenever what follows is a complete independent clause — this captures free latency gains that were being left on the table (e.g. 근데 이번에는, 그러면, 그럼 이제 cases).

[When to Segment]: added rule for splitting a -고 clause when both sides are independently complete clauses with their own subject+verb, distinguishing this from the verb-object dependency case where the object appears later.
[When to Segment]: added rule for splitting before a trailing opinion/nominalizer tail (-는 거 같애, -는 것 같다) when the preceding clause is already semantically complete.

[When to Segment]: sharpened the verb-object dependency guidance so the boundary is moved past the point where the verb's governed object/complement appears, rather than cut right after the connective, and similarly for chained causal connectives (-니까/-어서) and contrastive -는데 pairs, so the tag lands after the dependency is resolved instead of being omitted.

[Decision Procedure]: updated step 1 and step 6 to explicitly check for (a) a verb whose object/complement appears only in the following clause, (b) a chain of causal connectives that should be split only at the final link, (c) a contrastive -는데 clause that should stay paired with its contrast, and (d) a resolved sentence-initial discourse marker or adverbial followed by a full independent clause, which should now be treated as a valid free split point.
